w10_T4_004305: A gymnastics academy ordered 160 foam mats and shared them equally between its 5 halls; the blue hall's share is the one being followed. The blue hall then split its mats evenly into 2 identical stores, and only the upstairs store is counted from here on. Mice ruined 3 mats up there, and 5 more were lent to a school and never came back. A club that closed down donated 51 mats to the upstairs store. How many mats are in the upstairs store?
w10_T4_004306: A watchmaker had 67 movements in his drawer, and 28 of them were sold to a collector. Each movement still in the drawer needed 4 tiny springs. The supplier sent 3 springs for every spring on that list, to allow for breakages. The springs were divided evenly into 2 equal boxes, and the workshop box is the one being followed. During the year 54 springs from that box snapped, and the shop has been trading for 90 years. How many springs are in the workshop box?
w10_T4_004320: Ingrid grows more sunflowers than her neighbour Bo does. She started with 236 seedlings, and 157 were lost to slugs. Bo gave her 42 seedlings from his own tray. Every seedling she had left went on to produce 6 flower heads. Wind snapped 207 of the flower heads before the show. How many flower heads does Ingrid have?
w10_T4_004323: A hospital radio station had 149 records in its cabinet, and a listener donated 69 more. A burst pipe destroyed 197 records. The station then made 7 digital copies of every record that survived. A volunteer added 34 copies from her own collection, a college sent 45, and a local band contributed 35. Half of the cabinet is now taken up by cables. How many copies does the station have?
w10_T4_004328: A bus depot began the month with 158 timetable boards. The design team took 25 boards away to be redrawn. A printer delivered 51 new boards, and 17 boards were damaged by vandals. The council then ordered a complete set for each of the 7 routes, using that many boards per route. Half of the depot yard is given over to parking, and the timetables are printed in hours although the drivers work to minutes. How many boards were ordered altogether?
w10_T4_004329: A craft brewery had 169 empty kegs in its yard. The cooper then delivered 3 kegs for every keg the brewery already had. A pub chain took 394 kegs away. A festival returned 74 kegs, and a supermarket order removed 125 of them. A bar that was closing sold the brewery 73 kegs, and the brewhouse itself is 15 years old. How many kegs does the brewery have now?
w10_T4_004330: On Monday morning Ludo had 67 trays of bedding plants, more than his colleague Sanne had prepared. Each tray held 7 plants. Before noon 102 plants were sold. In the afternoon Sanne added 59 plants to the bench, and a delivery brought 51 more. In the evening head office ordered that same display for each of its 4 garden centres, needing that many plants per centre. The centres advertise opening times in hours although the staff rotas are written in minutes. How many plants are needed altogether?
w10_T4_004342: On Saturday morning a bike shop had 213 inner tubes in stock. A cycling club bought 203 tubes before lunch. In the early afternoon 9 tubes were found to be perished and were binned. In the evening the wholesaler delivered 5 tubes for every tube still in the shop. Overnight head office repeated that delivery at each of its 7 branches, sending that many tubes to every branch. The shop quotes repair times in minutes although its adverts give them in hours. How many tubes were sent to the branches altogether?
w10_T4_004343: On Sunday morning a bakery stall had 21 sourdough loaves, and the second oven load left it with 2 loaves for every loaf already on the table. At midday a neighbour brought 4 more loaves. During the afternoon 44 loaves were sold. In the evening a late customer bought 1 last loaf. How many loaves are left on the stall?
w10_T4_004345: Ottilie carves more spoons than her apprentice Nils does. She had 158 blocks of wood, and 56 of them were too knotty to use. Each usable block was cut into 9 spoon blanks. The blanks were shared equally between the 3 benches in the workshop, and Ottilie's bench is the one being followed. Every blank at her bench was then whittled into 8 small tasting spoons, and a craft fair sold 2085 of those spoons. How many spoons are left at Ottilie's bench?
w10_T4_004348: On Monday morning Kaito had 118 sheets of origami paper, more than his classmate Mira had brought. He used 17 sheets in the first lesson. At lunchtime Mira gave him 18 sheets of her own. During the afternoon workshop 88 sheets were used up. In the evening his teacher supplied 7 sheets for every sheet Kaito had left. How many sheets does Kaito have now?
w10_T4_004352: On Friday morning Bea had 216 jars of pickles on her shelves, more than her supplier Ferdi carried in his van. He delivered 55 jars before opening. During the morning 198 jars were sold, and in the early afternoon 52 jars went out to a restaurant. In the evening Ferdi restocked the shop with 6 jars for every jar still on the shelf. Bea's sister then added 79 jars she had made at home. How many jars are in the shop now?
w10_T4_004354: A village school had 223 exercise books in its store. The teachers handed out 152 books in September. Another 29 books were found damp and thrown away. The rest were shared equally between the 3 classrooms, and the year-two room is the one being followed. Over the term 7 books went missing from that room, and half of the store cupboard is used for sports kit. How many books are left in the year-two room?
w10_T4_004355: A stationery firm printed 89 sheets of stickers, and each sheet carried 4 stickers. A designer added 3 loose stickers, and a sample pack brought 52 more. The firm then produced that same set for each of its 4 regional offices, needing that many stickers per office. A last-minute order added 25 stickers. Half of the print room is taken up by the guillotine. How many stickers were produced in total?
w10_T4_004356: Yusuf lends out more board games than his colleague Petra does. His shelf held 134 games, and a donation added 69 more. Members borrowed 125 games over the holidays. Petra returned 6 games she had kept at home, a school gave 38, and a shop that was closing sent 60. The library opens 5 days a week. How many games are on Yusuf's shelf now?
w10_T4_004361: Tanya's cafe has more chairs than Oleg's cafe does. She started with 148 chairs, and 3 were broken in a storm. She lent 126 chairs to the village fete. Oleg returned 18 chairs he had borrowed in the spring, and a house clearance added 25 more. A restaurant then bought 42 chairs from her. The cafe holds each booking for 90 minutes, and the board shows bookings in hours although the till records them in minutes. How many chairs does Tanya have now?
w10_T4_004362: On Monday morning Alina cut 163 sheets of veneer, more than her partner Georg managed. Each sheet was sliced into 9 strips before noon. In the early afternoon every strip was cut into 7 tiles. Later 6074 tiles were laid on a hotel floor, and 1313 tiles cracked in the press. In the evening the factory produced 6 tiles for every tile still in the store. How many tiles are in the store now?
w10_T4_004367: A wildlife park had 132 nesting boxes on its trees. A gale brought down 4 boxes, 79 were moved to a new reserve, and 12 were taken away for repair. The trust then built 7 boxes for every box still standing in the park. Over the winter squirrels destroyed 114 boxes, and the park covers 300 hectares. How many nesting boxes does the park have now?
w10_T4_004368: Rafael prints more photographs than his assistant Nour does. He shot 75 rolls of film and bought 54 more from a colleague. Each roll produced 8 negatives, and every negative was printed at 7 different sizes. A flood in the darkroom ruined 539 prints. A gallery then ordered the whole surviving collection for each of its 4 venues, needing that many prints per venue. Half of the darkroom is unusable now, and the gallery has been open 22 years. How many prints does the gallery order come to?
w10_T4_004379: A repair cafe had 23 sewing machines. Volunteers took 11 machines to a school workshop, 9 were found to be beyond repair, and 1 was sold to a collector. A factory that closed then donated 63 machines. Half of the back room is used for storage. How many sewing machines does the repair cafe have now?
w10_T4_004381: On Wednesday morning a paint plant had 170 tins of base white, and 126 tins were used up on a hotel job. At midday a delivery doubled the number of tins in the store. During the afternoon the plant tinted 6 tins of colour from every tin of base. In the evening the depot ordered that whole batch for each of its 5 branches, needing that many tins per branch. The plant lists drying times in hours although the labels give them in minutes. How many tins were ordered altogether?
w10_T4_004388: A taxi firm had 47 airport vouchers in the office. Drivers used 39 vouchers on Friday. The airport issued 30 fresh vouchers, and 12 expired at the end of the month. A hotel returned 9 unused vouchers. The airport then matched the office's stock, leaving it with 2 vouchers for every voucher it held. The firm quotes waiting times in minutes although the contract is written in hours. How many vouchers does the office have now?
w10_T4_004413: Salim makes more board-game counters than his neighbour Dana does. His workshop cut 111 boards, and each board yielded 3 panels. Every panel was then punched into 6 counters. A drawer turned up 10 spare counters from an old set. A toy shop bought 593 counters, and the workshop's lathe is 40 years old. How many counters does Salim have?
w10_T4_004431: On Tuesday morning a glassworks had 128 rods of coloured glass, and the second furnace left it with 2 rods for every rod on the rack before noon. In the afternoon each rod was drawn out into 8 beads. In the early evening a supplier delivered 51 loose beads. Overnight a partner works matched the whole bench, leaving 2 beads for every bead on it. The furnace runs at 1100 degrees. How many beads are on the bench now?
w10_T4_004434: Elodie makes more lace panels than her cousin Theo does. She wove 122 lengths of thread, and each length produced 8 panels. A moth infestation ruined 495 panels. A museum commission then called for 9 copies of every panel she had left. A department store tripled that commission. The workshop has 16 looms. How many panels does the commission come to?
